title: Stratifying vascular disease patients into homogeneous subgroups using machine learning and FLAIR MRI biomarkers.
summary: Five imaging-defined groups showed distinct vascular and cerebral characteristics in the observed atherosclerosis cohort. The bibliographic records retrieved do not state an author affiliation.
ai_technology: K-means grouped regional FLAIR features, with a random forest identifying markers differentiating the groups.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: In 379 patients the groups differed in clinical and imaging measures, including vascular risks and white matter lesion burden.
evidence.unknown: Five imaging-defined groups showed distinct vascular and cerebral characteristics in the observed atherosclerosis cohort. Internal statistical comparison of reported clinical and lesion covariates supports exploratory cohort stratification. No independent replication or treatment effect was established.
evidence.ai_role: K-means grouped regional FLAIR features, with a random forest identifying markers differentiating the groups.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
